# Project-Wide Development Instructions

## My Development Preferences
- I primarily develop user interfaces using React.
- Use JavaScript or TypeScript according to manager-approved requirements.
- Explain technical concepts in beginner-friendly language.
- Prefer clear, maintainable and reusable code.

## Before Starting a Task
- Inspect the existing project structure and relevant files.
- Read existing documentation and configuration files.
- Identify the current framework, dependencies, package manager and styling system.
- Do not assume every project uses the same technology stack.
- Ask questions when essential requirements are missing.

## Technology Decisions
- Never assume JavaScript or TypeScript is approved.
- Never introduce a new UI library without checking project requirements.
- Follow the existing architecture and company coding standards.
- Do not invent API endpoints, design specifications or manager approvals.

## Code Changes
- Explain significant proposed changes before implementing them.
- Prefer small, focused changes.
- Do not overwrite existing work without approval.
- Never expose secrets, passwords, API keys or access tokens.
- Do not run destructive commands without explicit approval.

## Testing
- Recommend appropriate tests for every meaningful change.
- Explain how to verify the implementation.
- Report errors honestly instead of hiding them.
